body.en: Louis Fischer was an American journalist who met Gandhi and wrote The Life of Mahatma Gandhi. Indigo is an extract from that biography and describes the Champaran movement of 1917, partly in Gandhi's own words as Gandhi told them to Fischer. It is non-fiction: a biographical account of real events.

body.en: *Rajkumar Shukla* was a poor, illiterate sharecropper from Champaran in Bihar, near the foothills of the Himalayas. He came to the Congress session at Lucknow in December 1916 to ask Gandhi to visit Champaran. He followed Gandhi to Cawnpore, to his ashram near Ahmedabad and then to Calcutta, until Gandhi agreed. They went first to Patna, where at the house of the lawyer Rajendra Prasad the servants took Gandhi for another poor peasant. Then they went to Muzaffarpur, where Professor J. B. Kripalani received them.

Muzaffarpur: welcomed by Professor J. B. Kripalani

problem.en: How did Rajkumar Shukla show his determination?

steps.en: Describe his request at Lucknow in December 1916.
Show his persistence: he followed Gandhi from city to city.

answer.en: Rajkumar Shukla, a poor sharecropper, met Gandhi at the Lucknow Congress session and then followed him to Cawnpore, Ahmedabad and Calcutta, refusing to leave until Gandhi agreed to come to Champaran.
